versions.changelog: setup.sh: added Python 3 check (exits with clear message if missing), pip bootstrap before any pip install — tries ensurepip, then apt/yum/dnf/brew package managers, then falls back to get-pip.py from pypa.io. Upgrades pip to latest before installing packages. Works on fresh EC2 instances (Amazon Linux 2, Amazon Linux 2023, Ubuntu) with no pre-installed pip.

Auto-setup on install: added setup.sh (installs all Python packages + tesseract/ffmpeg via brew/apt), requirements.txt inside the skill directory, and Step 0 in SKILL.md that makes Claude run setup automatically before any script operation — no manual pip install needed after clawhub install. README updated: install section now shows 'clawhub install + bash setup.sh' as the two-step install; manual pip install section replaced with dependency table; clawhub run redact commands (which don't exist) replaced with direct python invocations.

Workflow fixes: removed non-existent 'clawhub run redact' commands from README (replaced with direct Python invocations); legal-redactor.md Step 5 now includes dry-run preview step, --custom flag documentation for ALL-CAPS names and positional PDF extraction gaps, verification step to re-extract text after redaction; Step 9 save options now covers PDF/image/text output types. Docs: SKILL.md and legal-redactor.md PII tables updated with unit number rule (#02-01, Unit 3B, Apt 4C) and BLK/BLOCK/FLAT street address prefix coverage added in v3.4.0.

Address redaction improvements: street address rule now covers BLK/BLOCK/FLAT/UNIT/APT/SUITE prefixes (e.g. 'BLK 101 Dalvey Road' redacted in full). New 'Unit number' rule covers apartment/unit notation: #02-01, Unit 3B, Apt 4C, Flat 12, etc. Card expiry false-positive fix: negative lookahead prevents matching the MM/DD part of MM/DD/YYYY transaction dates (e.g. 05/12 in 05/12/2025).

Major release: doc-scan skill merged into doc-process. New doc_scanner.py: multi-strategy edge detection (Canny + morphological gradient + colour/brightness), sub-pixel corner refinement, Lanczos perspective warp, improved shadow removal, scan-quality BW enhancement (adaptive threshold with auto block-size, stroke repair, denoising), auto white-background normalisation, scanner border. New references/doc-scan.md reference guide. SKILL.md fully rewritten with explicit documentation: complete feature table, full install instructions, all script deps, import verification table, full PII rule coverage (50+ rules), complete redaction mechanics, doc-scan pipeline, privacy policy, all modes and trigger phrases.

Major PII rule expansion for global document coverage. Cat1: UK NIN, Australian TFN & Medicare, Indian Aadhaar, UK NHS number, national/voter ID (keyword), VIN, IPv4, MAC address, PO Box, UK postcode, age keyword, expanded DOB (month-name dates), extended labeled-name keywords (50+ document field types: buyer/seller/tenant/plaintiff/employee/patient/shareholder etc). Cat2: card CVV, card expiry, UK sort code, Australian BSB, Indian IFSC, credit score, loan/mortgage amounts, tax figures, net worth, crypto wallet addresses, expanded salary keywords (CTC, gross/net pay, take-home, remuneration). Cat3: blood type, reproductive health, substance use (expanded), sexual orientation/gender identity, disability, criminal record, genetic information, trade secrets. Phone regex: added letter+hyphen lookbehind to prevent false positives on reference codes like DOC-2024-001.

Major PII rule improvements: added keyword-anchored name detection (Bill To, Shipper, Attention, etc.), Mr/Mrs/Dr title-prefix names, Indian PAN numbers, 6-digit international postal codes (Singapore/India), extended street types (Hl, Circle, Parkway etc.). Fixed: phone false positives on dates and cross-line decimals, IBAN false positives on non-country-code prefixes, ABA routing now matches 'ABA No.' label, SWIFT allows space within code value. Total invoice coverage improved from 12 to 23 items.
PDF redaction rewritten using rasterise-and-redact approach.

Complete rewrite of redaction. Output is always a copy of the original file — the original is never modified. PDFs get opaque black rectangles burned over PII (text permanently removed). Images get black bars via OCR+PIL. Text files get token replacement. Single entry point: redact_file(). Summary always printed showing what was redacted. 88 tests (248 total), all passing.

Visual black-bar redaction: PDFs get permanent black rectangles drawn over PII via PyMuPDF (text is unrecoverable); images get black bars via OCR+PIL (requires tesseract); text files unchanged. Auto-routes by file extension. Always prints structured redaction summary to stderr with per-category breakdown and item counts. Keyword rules (DOB, account, salary, etc.) preserve the label text and only black-out the value. 84 tests pass (2 skipped pending tesseract install).

Fix redactor: single-pass engine prevents nested token re-redaction; keyword rules now preserve label text; credit card beats phone in priority; password-protected file detection with helpful decrypt instructions; 89 new tests (250 total, all passing)

**Summary: Improved security and transparency for document processing.**

- Requires user confirmation before reading document content for categorization.
- New section details how each feature is implemented, highlighting that most do not use external libraries or scripts.
- Clear separation between core features (no install needed) and script-assisted modes (optional dependencies listed).
- Enhanced documentation of script imports and network requirements for full user auditability.
- Privacy and data handling section refocused for brevity and clarity.

**doc-process 2.1.0 Changelog**

- Added a dedicated Privacy & Data Handling section explaining local data usage, timeline consent, and script safety.
- Document timeline now requires explicit user opt-in per session; logs stored locally at `~/.doc-process-timeline.json`.
- Clarified that no document or personal data is stored or retained after the session unless user consents.
- All reference files, including for form autofill and timeline, updated to reflect privacy, local-only access, and consent-based behavior.
- General documentation improvements for transparency and clearer user instructions.

**Doc-Process 2.0.0 — Major update adds document auto-categorization and workflow streamlining**

- Added Document Categorizer: automatically classifies uploaded documents and routes to the correct mode if user intent is unclear.
- Expanded to 13 tasks: now includes document categorization and doc scan (clean scan/photo-to-PDF appearance) alongside existing modes.
- Improved workflow: skill now tries to identify document type before prompting for a mode, reducing user friction.
- Updated reference guides and trigger phrases throughout for all new modes.
- Enhanced existing modes with additional capabilities such as type inference, critical value alerts, and severity tiers.

**Major update: Expanded to eleven document tasks with new modes, scripts, and automation.**

- Added support for: resume/CV parsing, ID/passport scanning, medical summarization, legal redaction, meeting minutes extraction (including audio transcription), table/data extraction, document translation, and document timeline tracking.
- Introduced new reference guides and helper scripts for each new document mode.
- Document timeline step added: silently logs every processed document unless/until user requests timeline.
- Updated instructions for handling audio (meeting minutes) including automated transcription workflow.
- Refined general principles and usability details for sensitive data handling, disclaimers, and script usage.

Initial release of doc-process: a unified document intelligence skill for forms, contracts, receipts, and bank statements.

- Supports four modes: form autofill, contract analysis, receipt scanning, and bank statement analysis.
- Auto-detects user intent based on trigger phrases; asks clarifying questions if ambiguous.
- Integrates Python helper scripts for expense logging, statement parsing, and report generation.
- Guides user to upload a file if missing, supports reading PDFs in chunks for large documents.
- Presents results in clear tables and scannable summaries, protecting sensitive data and flagging risks when needed.
